sources.title: Benchmark Test-Time Scaling of General LLM Agents
sources.status: arXiv v1, primary study; reopened online
sources.use: Distinguishes oracle candidate coverage from actual selected-answer accuracy and documents context/verification limitations across agent domains.
sources.limit: Its independent trajectories/selection and unified tool environment are not our residual200k/30/30 policy. Point-wise conditional metric is not deployed selected-answer accuracy; no repository reproduction here.

sources.title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
sources.status: ICML2025 study; reopened primary arXiv version
sources.use: Different model or independent request does not guarantee independent errors; reported HELM wrong-answer agreement is conditional on both outputs being wrong.
sources.limit: Multiple-choice/model response study, not a measured error correlation for FHIR agents or proof of V7 failure cause.

sources.title: FineVerify: Scaling Test-Time Compute with Fine-Grained Self-Verification for Agentic Search
sources.status: arXiv v1; reopened online, algorithm sections2.1–2.4
sources.use: Shared question-derived checks and candidate evidence search motivate bounded targeted investigation.
sources.limit: Multiple candidates, search costs and model judgments differ from this project; no semantic proof, code reproduction, equal-budget transfer or reported gain inherited. Root code-audit caveats are separately attributed, not independently reread here.

sources.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
sources.use: Compute allocation effectiveness depends on tasks/difficulty and proposal/verifier behavior; cost must include the extra work.
sources.limit: Uses specialized MATH models/verifiers.2048-sample difficulty estimates and their omitted assessment costs do not provide an admissible free difficulty router for FHIR.

sources.title: The McNemar test for binary matched-pairs data: mid-p and asymptotic are better than exact conditional
sources.status: Primary statistical study, abstract reopened online
sources.use: Paired binary inference is governed by discordances; sparse outcomes/test choice affect power.
sources.limit: No proposal to replace patient-block bootstrap with unclustered McNemar. Planning formula in this memo is an explicit independent-pair variance derivation, not a patient-cluster power guarantee or recommendation from this paper.

sources.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
sources.use: Repeatedly optimizing finite noisy evaluation criteria can bias model/architecture selection even when model weights are not trained.
sources.limit: This motivates the workflow distinction; it does not numerically measure how much our current300 has overfit.

sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
sources.use: Adaptive ordinary holdout reuse is not independent validation; formal reusable-holdout mechanisms require their stated protections.
sources.limit: Our transparent scorer does not implement the paper’s algorithm or inherit its guarantees; reshuffling does not undo exposure.

sources.title: Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet?
sources.use: Fresh-test performance changes may reflect distribution difficulty rather than adaptive overfitting alone.
sources.limit: Image recognition evidence, not an estimate of FHIR transfer or justification to assume absence of adaptation bias.

sources.title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
sources.status: Nature Machine Intelligence2026 primary study, source reopened/search-verified
sources.use: 260 configurations across models/tasks support treating collaboration benefit as conditional on baseline/task/context and measuring actual overhead.
sources.limit: Its empirical~45% rule is not a universal causal threshold or permitted router here; controlled ceilings are not equal actual costs/FLOPs. No numerical code reproduction here.
